rationale: This program is a trivial 2-function, 55-byte hello binary where runtime is effectively free (a single print) and the main constraint is binary size bloat versus analysis resistance, so weights prioritize security/diversity dimensions while keeping RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights low to avoid disproportionate text-segment expansion of an already tiny image. SUB and IBR lead: instruction substitution is cheap, correctness-safe, and effective on straight-line printf-then-return code, and implicit basic-block reordering disrupts the trivially linear CFG of main without measurable runtime cost on a run-once program. ICALL and IGV are set high because a 2-function image gives analysts almost no cross-reference noise to work through, so indirect calls and inter-procedural variable hiding yield high marginal confusion per byte added. BCF gets a moderate weight — bogus control flow adds useful structural noise even in tiny functions, but its size Cost is damped to limit bloat. FLA and SPLIT are weighted lowest: main contains no loops to flatten and is too small for splitting to produce meaningful complexity, making both passes near-pure size overhead here. CorrectnessRisk weights are uniformly kept low so the selector remains free to apply passes safely to the straight-line, loop-free code, preserving print-output correctness.
